headline: A strong storm Wednesday night into Thanksgiving brings damaging-level gusts to the Strait of Juan de Fuca, the north interior and the coast, windy conditions around Puget Sound, more heavy rain and another round of coastal flooding, before a brief, showery break over the weekend.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: A front pushing onshore brings periods of rain and gusty showers Wednesday, then a warm front lifting north brings stronger rain and wind to the coast by early evening and across the interior overnight. A Wind Advisory runs from 4 PM Wednesday to 11 AM Thursday for the Eastern and Western Strait of Juan de Fuca (Sequim and Port Angeles), the Lake Crescent/US 101 area, Port Townsend, the San Juans, Island County, Everett, the Skagit and Whatcom lowlands and the coast, where gusts may reach 50 to 55 mph along the coast and in the north interior. Seattle, the Eastside, Kitsap, Tacoma, Olympia, Hood Canal and the Olympics are under a Wind Advisory from 8 PM Wednesday to noon Thursday, with Puget Sound gusts around 40 mph as the warm front moves inland early Thanksgiving morning. A Winter Storm Warning covers the Whatcom and Skagit Cascades from 7 PM Wednesday to 4 AM Friday.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Storm rainfall totals reach about 1 inch in the interior lowlands (less in the Olympic rain shadow around Sequim), up to 2 inches on the coast, 2 to 3 inches in the Cascades and 2 to 4 inches in the Olympics. A Flood Watch runs Wednesday morning through Sunday afternoon for the Olympics and their western and southern foothills, Olympia and southern Puget Sound, southern Hood Canal, the Chehalis Valley and the Willapa and Black Hills; no widespread river flooding is expected, but the Skokomish River in Mason County is on track to reach moderate flooding midweek. The trailing cold front sweeps inland Thursday afternoon, bringing showers, perhaps an isolated thunderstorm, and gradually easing winds. A weaker system arrives later Friday.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Weak high pressure may bring a brief break over the weekend, though it is hard to rule out rain for more than about 12 hours at a time. By early next week a broad dip in the jet stream sets up offshore and another series of storms marches onshore, keeping the weather unsettled.

coast: Some of the year's highest tides combined with storm surge and high surf keep coastal flooding as the top hazard through the end of the week. A Coastal Flood Warning runs 9 AM to 4 PM Wednesday for the Eastern and Western Strait of Juan de Fuca and the Washington coast (and until 10 AM Wednesday for San Juan County), a Coastal Flood Advisory covers Seattle, Everett, Kitsap, Port Townsend, Island County and other Sound shorelines until 9 AM Wednesday, and a Coastal Flood Watch runs late Wednesday night through Thursday afternoon for the Strait (including Sequim and Port Angeles), Port Townsend, the San Juans, Seattle, Everett, Kitsap, northern Hood Canal, the Pierce, King, Skagit and Whatcom lowlands and the coast. A High Surf Advisory covers the coast until 4 PM Wednesday. On the water, a Storm Warning covers all coastal waters and Gale Warnings cover the east and west entrances of the Strait of Juan de Fuca and the northern inland waters until 4 AM Thursday, with Small Craft Advisories for Admiralty Inlet, Puget Sound, Hood Canal and the Grays Harbor bar; an isolated thunderstorm is possible over the coastal waters Thursday afternoon. Coastal seas of 15 to 20 feet ease to 10 to 15 feet late Thursday into Friday and below 10 feet over the weekend, with a brief lull in wind Friday before weekend systems may stir things up again.
watch_for: Strongest winds Wednesday night into Thursday morning along the Strait, north interior and coast (50–55 mph gusts)
Coastal flooding at Thursday's high tides along the Strait, the Sound and the coast
Skokomish River flooding in Mason County and possible flooding in the Flood Watch area through Sunday
confidence: Confidence is fairly high for the Wednesday night–Thursday storm, with the overall picture and rain totals little changed from earlier forecasts, but the weekend break looks brief and uncertain before more storms next week.
